title: How soap cleans
examples: What makes soap able to clean things?
How does soap get oil off my hands?
Are soap molecules attracted to water or oil?

explain.say: Today we are learning how soap cleans things for us.
Soap molecules have two different parts that like different things.
The water-loving part of the soap likes to surround itself with water molecules.
The oil-loving part of the soap sticks right into the oil or grease it finds.
When soap surrounds oil, it forms a tiny ball called a micelle.
In real life, when you wash your hands, the soap forms these micelles around dirt.

faq.a: Soap works because one end of the molecule loves water and the other end loves oil.
asks: What is the job of soap?
How does soap clean oily messes?

faq.a: A micelle is a tiny ball structure formed when soap traps dirt or oil inside it.
asks: How is the dirt held by soap?

faq.q: Does soap need water to work?
faq.a: Yes, soap needs water because the water-loving parts of the soap need water to stay suspended.
asks: Is water necessary for cleaning with soap?

faq.q: Are all cleaning agents like soap?
faq.a: Not all cleaning agents work the same way; soap has specific parts that attract different substances.
asks: Is soap the only thing that cleans?
Do other cleaners act like soap?

faq.q: What are the two parts of a soap molecule?
faq.a: The two parts are the head, which loves water, and the tail, which loves oil.
asks: What are the ends of a soap molecule?

facts: Soap molecules have two distinct ends.
One end is hydrophilic, meaning it loves water.
The other end is hydrophobic, meaning it loves oil.
When soap cleans, it traps dirt in structures called micelles.

quiz.say: If soap is cleaning oil, which part of the molecule is doing the work?
quiz.why: The hydrophobic tail is oil-loving, so it sticks to the grease.

wrong.1: This part loves water, so it would push the oil away.
wrong.2: The molecule has two parts, and only one part targets the oil.
wrong.3: Water is the liquid, not the part that sticks to the oil.

quiz.say: What is the structure formed when soap traps dirt?
quiz.why: The micelle is the name for the soap ball that holds the dirt.

wrong.0: A solution means everything is mixed evenly, but the dirt is trapped.
wrong.2: A soap bubble is just soap film, not a dirt trap.
wrong.3: While related, micelle specifically describes the soap-dirt trap.

quiz.say: If soap is in water, which part of the molecule faces the water?
quiz.why: The hydrophilic head is defined as the part that loves water.

wrong.1: This tail part is designed to avoid water and stick to oil.
wrong.2: The center holds the oil, not the part that touches the water.
wrong.3: The head is the specific part that interacts with the water.
